source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's SAT1 campus in San Antonio publishes 9 MW of IT capacity, and that single figure is the only power number attached to the site.

The pattern here is disclosure, not size. Texas holds 137 mapped facilities, and only 19 of them publish a megawatt figure at all, totaling 475.41 MW. SAT1 ranks 14th in the state by published megawatts, which places it in the middle of a disclosed subset that is roughly one seventh of the state's mapped footprint. The 110,000 square feet of technical space and the six certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II and TIA-942, describe what the building is qualified to host, not how much compute it runs.

For AI specifically, the 9 MW is the whole story the record supports. Converting it to racks or accelerators requires assuming a density the operator never states, so any GPU count derived from it is a modeling choice rather than a disclosed specification. What the figure does establish is the ceiling: whatever silicon sits inside SAT1, it draws against 9 MW of published IT load, and that is the same binding constraint that applies at every other campus on this record.

The data does not say who the tenants are, how many racks are installed, or whether the campus is fully leased. It also does not cover announced expansion, which the suitability inputs list as missing. A 14th-place rank within 19 disclosing facilities is not a rank within Texas's full buildout, and it should not be read as one.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
